manual.title: Negotiating With Geese
manual.subtitle: Field tactics for parks, golf courses and office campuses
manual.voice: A wildlife-conflict consultant with nineteen nesting seasons on golf courses, corporate lawns and municipal ponds, who writes in the calm, measured register of a professional hostage negotiator. Geese are “the other party”, a charging gander is “an escalation” and a site plan is “a settlement”. The diplomatic vocabulary is played completely straight, and the dry humour comes from that. Underneath it is real field biology: postures, seasons, distances in metres, what each deterrent costs and how long it lasts. Respects the birds as rational actors with clear interests. Firm on two points: never harm a goose, and never touch a nest or eggs without the permit the law requires.
